subject.title: [Feature]: Keep Codex app-server with Gateway for remote execution

question: Should OpenClaw accept an experimental Codex remote-execution mode that keeps Gateway and the Codex app-server co-located over stdio while routing execution to an authenticated registry-backed exec-server environment?
rationale: The issue proposes new plugin configuration, SecretRef credential handling, remote filesystem/process execution, thread identity semantics, and fail-closed security policy that cleanup automation cannot approve as product direction.

options.title: Review the linked PR as canonical
options.body: Use https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/101326 as the implementation candidate and decide whether its experimental config, security boundary, and compatibility behavior are acceptable.

options.title: Hold as a design issue
options.body: Keep implementation paused until maintainers narrow the topology, upgrade policy, and remote-executor trust model.

options.title: Reject the core/plugin surface
options.body: Close this direction and the linked PR if maintainers decide this remote execution topology should stay outside OpenClaw for now.

recommendation.title: Review the linked PR as canonical
recommendation.body: Use https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/101326 as the implementation candidate and decide whether its experimental config, security boundary, and compatibility behavior are acceptable.

likelyOwner.reason: They authored the design issue, are assigned to the linked implementation PR, and have recent merged history on the Codex app-server lifecycle surface involved in the decision.
